claims.statement: EU Regulation 2023/1542 requires, from 18 February 2027, an electronic battery passport for each LMT battery, EV battery, and industrial battery above 2 kWh placed on the market or put into service.
The passport is accessed through a QR code linked to a unique identifier, with different information access categories including public, authority, and legitimate-interest access.
The economic operator placing the battery on the market is responsible for ensuring passport information is accurate, complete, and up to date.

contrary_evidence: The passport obligation targets specified categories rather than every battery, and the above-2-kWh threshold narrows the stationary segment.
The regulation assigns accuracy responsibility to the economic operator, which may make operators reluctant to depend on a young vendor.
The 2027 start date gives OEMs and larger industrial platforms time to bundle their own solutions.

economics.acquisition_route: Use the family renewable installer to map the storage value chain, then target 3 private-label or assembler design partners and partner with storage distributors
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated 5-8 year scenario: 60 manufacturers averaging 100,000 PLN annual recurring and usage revenue yields 6.0m PLN; at 30% EBITDA, 4x, and 75% ownership, equity value is about 5.4m PLN.
economics.founder_time: 20-25 hours per week through the first integration, falling after templates and partner onboarding are standardized
economics.gross_margin_basis: Identifier issuance, data validation, and hosting are software-like; bespoke ERP/BMS integration and data remediation are the main margin leaks
economics.payback: Customer payback hypothesis: one shared passport layer can replace custom build and duplicate warranty/service records; compare total annual cost against internal engineering and recall support in pilots
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: 20,000-60,000 PLN setup per manufacturer, 8-30 PLN per unit annually, and paid lifecycle modules for service or warranty teams
economics.retention_or_repeat: Passports persist with assets, new units are continually issued, and service/warranty events make migration costly if data portability and trust are handled well

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Longitudinal unit histories and normalized service/failure events can improve warranty triage, second-life decisions, and buyer trust when customers permit aggregate learning
fingerprint.customer: EU stationary-storage battery assemblers, importers, and private-label operators placing industrial batteries above 2 kWh on the market
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label distribution through battery assemblers, energy-storage installers, import compliance firms, and the founder's family renewable-energy network for discovery
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Data templates, validation, access-control policy, unique-ID/QR issuance, immutable change history, and APIs for BMS/service partners; hypothesis 20,000-60,000 PLN integration plus 8-30 PLN per active unit per year
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Product or compliance lead pays integration and model onboarding, then per-unit issuance and annual active-passport hosting
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Preparing products for the February 2027 passport requirement, launching a model, commissioning units, or needing auditable lifecycle updates

founder_fit: Directly leverages the parents' renewable-energy installation context for workflow access without assuming customer commitments
Fits data modeling, sensor interest, anomaly detection, and asset-lifecycle analytics
Can begin as software and data operations rather than hardware inventory
A white-label infrastructure model minimizes personal-brand and high-volume social demands
risks: Battery makers or major ecosystem platforms may provide passports themselves
Incorrect or stale safety and composition data could create serious liability
Long-lived hosting creates security, continuity, and data-portability obligations
Standards and delegated specifications may change implementation details before the deadline

structure.commercial_archetype: Per-asset digital passport infrastructure with annual hosting and lifecycle-event fees
structure.control_point: The persistent QR-resolved electronic record that must exist for each covered battery placed on the market or put into service
structure.critical_dependency: Accurate manufacturer/BMS composition and performance data, stable identifier standards, and authority to maintain the passport throughout the battery lifecycle

thesis: Planning-stage hypothesis: provide a hosted battery-passport and lifecycle-data service for EU economic operators placing stationary industrial batteries above 2 kWh on the market, beginning with smaller storage assemblers, importers, and private-label brands underserved by automotive-scale platforms. The product would issue standards-compatible unique identifiers and QR destinations, validate model and unit data, enforce access tiers, and preserve updates from commissioning through repair, second life, and recycling. The passport URL becomes a durable control point attached to each unit; recurring value can expand from initial compliance into warranty, service, residual-value, and recall records.
title: Stationary-Battery Passport Operator
uncertainties: Number of addressable smaller EU battery economic operators not already tied to a passport vendor
Who legally controls updates when batteries are resold, repaired, repurposed, or recycled
Willingness of OEMs and BMS suppliers to expose unit-level performance data
Viable per-unit price and minimum annual contract size
